# Resource upgrade

This topic describes how to upgrade API gateway Kubernetes resource types when a Consul release requires it.

## Overview

Consul 2.0.0 introduced API gateway resource types in the `consul.hashicorp.com`
API group. These resource types improve compatibility with OpenShift Container
Platform (OCP) 4.19 and later, and support `TCPRoute` in environments where the
platform manages Gateway CRDs.

Consul 2.1 upgrades the Standard API gateway to the Kubernetes Gateway API v1.6
CRDs in the `gateway.networking.k8s.io` API group. These CRDs include `TCPRoute`. Refer to
[Upgrade steps](#upgrade-steps) for the Helm values to use for your platform.
The CRD version alone does not determine whether the Standard API gateway
controller watches `TCPRoute`. On OCP 4.19 and later, use the Consul API gateway
when the cluster uses `TCPRoute`.

## Requirements

- A Consul deployment in Kubernetes.

### Prerequisites

- `kubectl` tool should be instaleld for non-OCP clusters and `oc` for OCP clusters.
- Back up `Gateways`, `HTTPRoutes`, `TCPRoutes`, and `ReferenceGrants` in your cluster.
  For example, run the following commands to create namespace-level, resource-specific backup files:

<Tabs>

<Tab heading="OCP">

```shell-session
$ mkdir -p gateway-resource-backup && \
  for ns in $(oc get ns -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'); do \
    oc get gateways -n "$ns" -o yaml > "gateway-resource-backup/${ns}-gateways.yaml"; \
    oc get httproutes -n "$ns" -o yaml > "gateway-resource-backup/${ns}-httproutes.yaml"; \
    oc get tcproutes -n "$ns" -o yaml > "gateway-resource-backup/${ns}-tcproutes.yaml"; \
    oc get referencegrants -n "$ns" -o yaml > "gateway-resource-backup/${ns}-referencegrants.yaml"; \
  done
```

</Tab>

<Tab heading="Non-OCP">

```shell-session
$ mkdir -p gateway-resource-backup && \
  for ns in $(kubectl get ns -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'); do \
    kubectl get gateways -n "$ns" -o yaml > "gateway-resource-backup/${ns}-gateways.yaml"; \
    kubectl get httproutes -n "$ns" -o yaml > "gateway-resource-backup/${ns}-httproutes.yaml"; \
    kubectl get tcproutes -n "$ns" -o yaml > "gateway-resource-backup/${ns}-tcproutes.yaml"; \
    kubectl get referencegrants -n "$ns" -o yaml > "gateway-resource-backup/${ns}-referencegrants.yaml"; \
  done
```

</Tab>

</Tabs>


### Additional info

- If you use GoDaddy or Route53 as your DNS provider and have a CNAME record pointing to the API gateway, update that CNAME record when switching from the Standard API gateway to the Consul API gateway.
- When you upgrade to Consul 2.0, Consul automatically generates and applies manifests based on your gateway selection:
  - **Standard API gateway**: Consul generates manifests updated to the `v1` version of the `gateway.networking.k8s.io` API group and applies them.
  - **Consul API gateway**: Consul generates and applies manifests for both the Standard API gateway and the Consul API gateway, creating both gateways simultaneously. This gives you time to update your CNAME record in your DNS provider (such as GoDaddy or Route53) before decommissioning the Standard API gateway.


## Upgrade scenarios

If your cluster does not use `TCPRoute`, you can keep existing gateway resources.
If your cluster uses `TCPRoute`, upgrade to the new API group in one of these cases:

- OCP clusters that use `TCPRoute` and upgrade from OCP 4.18 to 4.19 or later.

  Move to the `consul.hashicorp.com` API group to maintain compatibility with OCP 4.19 and later.

- Non-OCP Kubernetes clusters that use `TCPRoute` and platform-managed Gateway CRDs earlier than v1.6.0.

  Move to the `consul.hashicorp.com` API group to maintain compatibility. If the platform manages Gateway CRDs v1.6.0 or later, the CRDs support `TCPRoute`, and you can keep using the Standard API gateway with `global.crds.enableTcpRoute` set to `true`.

## OpenShift Container Platform (OCP) upgrade steps

The upgrade process

To prepare for an OCP upgrade from 4.18 to 4.19+ you can follow these steps:

1. Make sure the OCP cluster s running OCP 4.18 or earlier and the target version is OCP 4.19 or later.
1. Verify Consul is deployed in the Cluster
1. Validate if the gateway CRDs under API group `gateway.networking.k8s.io` are pre-installed in the cluster. If pre-installed, set `global.installK8sNetworkingCRDs: false`.  
1. Make sure Gateway-related resources are backed up before the upgrade.

The backup and upgrade process involves these resource types:

- `Gateway`
- `HTTPRoute`
- `TCPRoute`
- `ReferenceGrant`

After all the preparations are complete, use the flowchart to identify the specific steps for your upgrade.

![Dual gateway new installation of Consul and OCP upgrade flow](/img/ocp-upgrade.png)

Finally, follow the steps in the section below according to your configuration.


## Upgrade steps

Starting in Consul 2.1, the Standard API gateway uses the Kubernetes Gateway API v1.6 CRDs in the `gateway.networking.k8s.io` API group. These CRDs include `TCPRoute`. Select the upgrade flow that matches your platform, and then run `helm upgrade` with the values for your configuration.

The first `helm upgrade` in each flow sets `global.generateManifests` to `true`. After the manifests are generated and you back them up, set it to `false` for subsequent Helm upgrades.

Before you upgrade, check whether you use `TCPRoute` and which Gateway CRD version your cluster has. On OCP clusters, use `oc` instead of `kubectl`.

1. Check for `TCPRoute` resources.

   ```shell-session
   $ kubectl get tcproutes -A
   ```

   If the command returns `error: the server doesn't have a resource type "tcproutes"`, the `TCPRoute` CRD is not installed and your cluster does not use `TCPRoute`. If the command returns `No resources found`, the CRD is installed but you have no `TCPRoute` resources.

1. Check the Gateway CRD version.

   ```shell-session
   $ kubectl get crd gateways.gateway.networking.k8s.io -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.gateway\.networking\.k8s\.io/bundle-version}'
   v1.6.1
   ```

   The command returns the Gateway API version of the installed CRDs. If the command returns an empty value, the CRDs do not have the `bundle-version` annotation. Refer to your platform documentation for the installed Gateway API version. If the command returns `NotFound`, the Gateway CRDs are not installed in your cluster.

### OpenShift upgrade from 4.18 to 4.19+

1. Run `helm upgrade` with one of the following `values.yaml` configurations as per requirement.

    <Tabs>

    <Tab heading="No TCP Route - Use Standard API gateway">

    <CodeBlockConfig filename="values.yaml">

    ```yaml
    global:
      installK8sNetworkingCRDs: true
      generateManifests: true
      openshift:
        enabled: true
        crds:
          enableTcpRoute: false
    ```

    </CodeBlockConfig>

    </Tab>

    <Tab heading="Require TCP Route - Use Consul API gateway">

    <CodeBlockConfig filename="values.yaml">

    ```yaml
    global:
      installK8sNetworkingCRDs: true
      generateManifests: true
      openshift:
        enabled: true
        crds:
          enableTcpRoute: true
          consulapi:
            enabled: true
    ```

    </CodeBlockConfig>

    </Tab>

    </Tabs>

1. Verify the access to the application.

   - **Standard API gateway**
   
     Verify access to the application through the gateway.

     ```shell-session
     $ oc get cgtw -A

      NAMESPACE   NAME                 CLASS                 ADDRESS   PROGRAMMED   AGE
      consul      api-gateway-consul   consul-custom-class             True         72m
     ```

   - **Consul API gateway**

     ```shell-session
     $ oc get gtw -A

      NAMESPACE   NAME          CLASS    ADDRESS   PROGRAMMED   AGE
      consul      api-gateway   consul             True         3d19h
     ```

     - You may see two gateways initially. Verify application access through both gateways.
     - Update your DNS (for example, Route53) to point to Consul DNS.

1. Back up generated manifests from the PVC.

1. Follow the OpenShift documentation to complete the platform upgrade, including:

   - Deleting Gateway CRDs.
   - Approving `adminAck`, if required.

1. Verify the access to the application after platform upgrade.

   - **Standard API gateway**
     - Apply the copied manifests taken from step 3.
     - After the gateway is ready, verify application access.
   - **Consul API gateway**
     - Verify application access.
     - If application access fails, run `helm upgrade` with:

        ```yaml
        global:
          installK8sNetworkingCRDs: false
          openshift:
            enabled: true
            upgradeTo419From418: false
            crds:
              enableTcpRoute: false
              consulapi:
                enabled: true
        ```
 
### OpenShift upgrade flow: platform upgrade not involved

Use this flow when you upgrade Consul and do not upgrade the OCP platform. If you are upgrading OCP from 4.18 to 4.19+, follow [OpenShift upgrade from 4.18 to 4.19+](#openshift-upgrade-from-418-to-419) instead. The `upgradeTo419From418` flag applies only to that flow. Refer to [`upgradeTo419From418`](/consul/docs/reference/k8s/helm#v-global-openshift-upgradeto419from418) for details.

On OCP 4.19 and later, set `global.openshift.crds.enableTcpRoute` to `false` when you use the `gateway.networking.k8s.io` CRDs. The Standard API gateway controller does not watch `TCPRoute` on these OCP versions, even when OCP provides v1.6 or later CRDs. Use the Consul API gateway when your cluster uses `TCPRoute`; use the Standard API gateway when it does not.

| OCP version | OCP Gateway CRD version | TCPRoute | Gateway | Action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4.18 or earlier | Not applicable | Used | Standard API gateway | Set `global.installK8sNetworkingCRDs` to `true` and `global.openshift.crds.enableTcpRoute` to `true`. |
| 4.18 or earlier | Not applicable | Not used | Standard API gateway | Set `global.installK8sNetworkingCRDs` to `true` and `global.openshift.crds.enableTcpRoute` to `false`. |
| 4.19 or later | v1.6 or later | Used | Consul API gateway | Set `global.openshift.enabled` and `global.openshift.isOcpGreaterthan4_18` to `true`. Set `global.installK8sNetworkingCRDs` and `global.openshift.crds.enableTcpRoute` to `false`, and `global.openshift.crds.consulapi.enabled` to `true`. |
| 4.19 or later | v1.6 or later | Not used | Standard API gateway | Set `global.openshift.enabled` and `global.openshift.isOcpGreaterthan4_18` to `true`. Set `global.installK8sNetworkingCRDs`, `global.openshift.crds.enableTcpRoute`, and `global.openshift.crds.consulapi.enabled` to `false`. |
| 4.19 or later | Earlier than v1.6 | Used | Consul API gateway | Set `global.openshift.enabled` and `global.openshift.isOcpGreaterthan4_18` to `true`. Set `global.installK8sNetworkingCRDs` and `global.openshift.crds.enableTcpRoute` to `false`, and `global.openshift.crds.consulapi.enabled` to `true`. |
| 4.19 or later | Earlier than v1.6 | Not used | Standard API gateway | Set `global.openshift.enabled` and `global.openshift.isOcpGreaterthan4_18` to `true`. Set `global.installK8sNetworkingCRDs`, `global.openshift.crds.enableTcpRoute`, and `global.openshift.crds.consulapi.enabled` to `false`. |

1. Run `helm upgrade` with one of the following `values.yaml` configurations.

    <Tabs>

    <Tab heading="OCP 4.18 or earlier, TCPRoute used">

    <CodeBlockConfig filename="values.yaml">

    ```yaml
    global:
      installK8sNetworkingCRDs: true
      generateManifests: true
      openshift:
        enabled: true
        crds:
          enableTcpRoute: true
    ```

    </CodeBlockConfig>

    </Tab>

    <Tab heading="OCP 4.18 or earlier, no TCPRoute">

    <CodeBlockConfig filename="values.yaml">

    ```yaml
    global:
      installK8sNetworkingCRDs: true
      generateManifests: true
      openshift:
        enabled: true
        crds:
          enableTcpRoute: false
    ```

    </CodeBlockConfig>

    </Tab>

    <Tab heading="OCP 4.19 or later, no TCPRoute - Standard API gateway">

    <CodeBlockConfig filename="values.yaml">

    ```yaml
    global:
      installK8sNetworkingCRDs: false
      generateManifests: true
      openshift:
        enabled: true
        isOcpGreaterthan4_18: true
        crds:
          enableTcpRoute: false
          consulapi:
            enabled: false
    ```

    </CodeBlockConfig>

    </Tab>

    <Tab heading="OCP 4.19 or later, TCPRoute used - Consul API gateway">

    <CodeBlockConfig filename="values.yaml">

    ```yaml
    global:
      installK8sNetworkingCRDs: false
      generateManifests: true
      openshift:
        enabled: true
        isOcpGreaterthan4_18: true
        crds:
          enableTcpRoute: false
          consulapi:
            enabled: true
    ```

    </CodeBlockConfig>

    </Tab>

    </Tabs>

1. Verify application access through the gateway.

1. Back up generated manifests from the PVC.

### Non-OCP upgrade flow: platform upgrade not involved

1. Run `helm upgrade` with one of the following `values.yaml` configurations.

  <Tabs>

  <Tab heading="Gateway CRDs are not managed by platform, TCPRoute used">

  <CodeBlockConfig filename="values.yaml">

  ```yaml
  global:
    installK8sNetworkingCRDs: true
    generateManifests: true
    crds:
      enableTcpRoute: true
  ```

  </CodeBlockConfig>

  </Tab>

  <Tab heading="Gateway CRDs are not managed by platform, no TCPRoute">

  <CodeBlockConfig filename="values.yaml">

  ```yaml
  global:
    installK8sNetworkingCRDs: true
    generateManifests: true
    crds:
      enableTcpRoute: false
  ```

  </CodeBlockConfig>

  </Tab>

  <Tab heading="Gateway CRDs are managed by platform">

  <CodeBlockConfig filename="values.yaml">

  ```yaml
  global:
    installK8sNetworkingCRDs: false
    generateManifests: true
    crds:
      enableTcpRoute: true
  ```

  </CodeBlockConfig>

  </Tab>

  </Tabs>

1. Verify application access.

  Access the application using the Standard API gateway.

1. Back up generated manifests from the PVC.

### Non-OCP upgrade flow: platform upgrade involved

This section assumes the current platform version does not manage Gateway CRDs,
and the upgraded platform version does.

1. Run `helm upgrade` with one of the following `values.yaml` configurations.

  <Tabs>

  <Tab heading="No TCPRoute required - Standard API gateway">

  <CodeBlockConfig filename="values.yaml">

  ```yaml
  global:
    installK8sNetworkingCRDs: true
    generateManifests: true
    crds:
      enableTcpRoute: false
  ```

  </CodeBlockConfig>

  </Tab>

  <Tab heading="TCPRoute required - Consul API gateway">

  <CodeBlockConfig filename="values.yaml">

  ```yaml
  global:
    installK8sNetworkingCRDs: true
    generateManifests: true
    crds:
      enableTcpRoute: true
      consulapi:
        enabled: true
  ```

  </CodeBlockConfig>

  </Tab>

  </Tabs>

1. Verify access to the application.

   - **Standard API gateway**
     Verify access to the application through the gateway.
   - **Consul API gateway**
     - You may see two gateways initially. Verify access through both gateways.
     - Update your DNS (for example, Route53) to point to Consul DNS.
     - Delete the Standard API gateway and related objects.

1. Back up generated manifests from the PVC.

1. Upgrade the platform following the official documentation of the platform.

1. Verify access to the application.

   - **Standard API gateway**
   
     Verify access to the application through the gateway.
   - **Consul API gateway**

     - Verify access to the application through the gateway.
     - If the application is not accessible, run `helm upgrade` with:

        ```yaml
        global:
          installK8sNetworkingCRDs: false
          crds:
            enableTcpRoute: false
            consulapi:
              enabled: true
        ```

## Rollback

### Rollback from Consul 2.x to 1.9 or earlier than 1.8.14

There are two ways to roll back using Helm.

**Option 1 — Direct version rollback**

Run the `helm rollback` command to roll back to a previous release directly.

```shell-session
$ helm rollback --force-conflicts <release-number>
```

**Option 2 — Explicit Helm values rollback**

1. Export the Helm values from the target version you want to roll back to.

   This example uses version `1.9.4`.

   ```shell-session
   $ helm show values hashicorp/consul --version 1.9.4 > values.yaml
   ```

1. Update all relevant fields in `values.yaml` as needed.

1. Run the `helm upgrade` command to upgrade to the target version using the updated values file.

   ```shell-session
   $ helm upgrade --install <release-name> hashicorp/consul \
       --version 1.9.4 \
       --namespace <namespace> \
       --values values.yaml \
       --force-conflicts
   ```
